chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who had a female slave under his ownership, so he divorced her according to the Sunnah, and she became independent from him, then he bought her back after that before she married another husband.
He said: 'Is it not that Ali (peace be upon him) ruled in this matter that a verse made it permissible and another verse made it forbidden?'
And I prohibit myself and my children from it.

key_terms.طَلَّقَهَا عَلَى السُّنَّةِ: Divorced her according to the Sunnah (proper procedure)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on repurchasing a freed female slave after divorcing her if she has not yet married another man?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the juristic nuance of *ibna al-milk* (ownership of a slave one has previously freed and repurchased) through Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) reference to Imam Ali’s (AS) ruling. The Imam notes that while Quranic verses provide both permissive and prohibitive bases for this transaction, he personally forbade it for himself and his progeny, illustrating the principle of *zawabit* (precautionary prohibition) in Shia fiqh to avoid potential legal ambiguities.
